newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures end up, trade quiet late.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures end up, trade quiet late.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures ended higher, after September Treasury bond futures hit a fresh four-month high late in the day.
Traders said the rally was fueled by hedge fund buying and short-covering ahead of options expiration.
July T-bond options expired at midday, with heavy open interest outstanding in calls sparking short-covering in the futures pit, traders said.
September T-bonds reached 112-24/32 on the rally, surpassing resistance at 112-16/32. A ceiling at 112-28/32, however, went unchallenged.
Several technicians put their near-term targets at the year's high of 113-9/32, set February 18. Others said the market may be overbought and need to trade sideways or correct before the next leg up.
Trade turned quiet late in the session, with traders said to be taking to the sidelines before the weekend.
The data line-up Friday was slim. There was scant reaction to U.S. May Fed budget deficit, which fell to $48.5 billion, down 8.6 percent from May 1996.
Trade in the short end remained within recent parameters.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 11/32 at 112-17/32, December Eurodollars were up 0.010 pts at 93.96, and 10-year notes were up 5/32 to 108-23/32. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
